coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: You're 27 days out and in taper—this is a long-run day, but keep it honest. Your recovery score is 46/100 (moderate) and your resting HR is elevated 7.5 bpm above your 30-day average at 74 bpm, which tells me you're still carrying fatigue from the peak block. Run 90–100 minutes at Z2 (130–140 bpm based on your recent work) with 600–800 ft of vert, focusing on smooth footfall and downhill control on technical terrain. This is sharpness maintenance, not a statement run. Skip the intensity.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You haven't run since August 13th—nine days ago—so your glycogen stores are replete but your GI system may be rusty. Pre-run: eat 30–40g carbs + 10–15g protein 90 minutes before. During the 90-minute run: carry 200–250 calories (sports drink, gels, or both) and 300–400mg sodium to rehearse your race fueling under real load. Post-run: 20g protein + 60g carbs within 30 minutes, then a full meal 2–3 hours later. The Julian Alps will demand precision nutrition at sparse aid stations—use every taper week run to dial this in.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your sleep efficiency is solid at 70%, but at 8.3 hours, you're sleeping enough volume without the depth you need in taper. Tonight, aim for 9 hours in a cool, dark room (ideally 62–65°F). Your elevated resting HR suggests your nervous system is still in sympathetic dominance—prioritize sleep over any other recovery modality. No ice baths, no extra mobility work today. Sleep is the only taper tool that matters right now. Get to bed by 10 pm if you can.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the psychologically hardest phase: fit enough to hurt, but forced to hold back. This 90-minute run will feel easy—that's the point. Use it to rehearse the mental tactics you'll need at kilometer 35 when the altitude and vert hit hard: controlled breathing, positive self-talk, and the knowledge that you've already done the hard work. The race is won in the taper by staying patient. Trust the plan, not the nervousness.
